THEO.01.note: Yale's Thessalonians course models how Pauline letters are read as occasional correspondence and directly addresses chronology, community setting, and disputed authorship.

exercise.prompt: Choose one Pauline letter and outline its sender, recipients, occasion, major argument, and current scholarly authorship status.

THEO.02.note: The Stanford entry provides the broader philosophical history of hermeneutics and the disciplined interpretation of texts, meaning, context, and understanding.

exercise.prompt: Interpret one short biblical passage in three stages: historical-literary context, textual claim, and contemporary application, keeping the stages distinct.

THEO.03.note: Yale's course treats canon formation historically, including the gradual recognition of texts and differences between communities rather than a single one-time decision.

exercise.prompt: Build a timeline of major Hebrew Bible and New Testament canon milestones, noting where different Christian traditions retain different collections.

THEO.04.note: Bible.org's scholarly overview lays out the literary relationships among Matthew, Mark, and Luke and compares the main proposed source theories.

exercise.prompt: Place one triple-tradition passage from Matthew, Mark, and Luke side by side and mark identical wording, omissions, additions, and changed order.

THEO.05.note: CSNTM explains why manuscripts matter and provides a concrete entry into the surviving witnesses that textual critics compare.

article.title: Why Manuscripts?
article.source: Center for the Study of New Testament Manuscripts

exercise.prompt: Compare two textual variants using manuscript age, geographical spread, transcriptional difficulty, and internal context; then defend a preferred reading.

THEO.06.note: The Israel Antiquities Authority introduces the discovery, date range, languages, contents, and significance of the Dead Sea Scrolls.

article.title: Introduction to the Dead Sea Scrolls
article.source: Leon Levy Dead Sea Scrolls Digital Library — Israel Antiquities Authority

exercise.prompt: Sort examples of scrolls into biblical manuscripts, apocryphal works, and sectarian writings, then explain what each category can and cannot establish.

THEO.07.note: The Israel Antiquities Authority's historical background places the scrolls within Hellenistic and Roman Judea and the diverse Jewish groups of the Second Temple period.

article.title: Historical Background
article.source: Leon Levy Dead Sea Scrolls Digital Library — Israel Antiquities Authority

exercise.prompt: Create a comparison chart for Pharisees, Sadducees, Essenes, revolutionary movements, and the early Jesus movement, including sources and uncertainties.

THEO.08.note: This historian-written overview uses Nicaea and Chalcedon to show how imperial politics, episcopal authority, and precise Christological language interacted in the councils.

exercise.prompt: Make a council table for Nicaea, Constantinople, Ephesus, and Chalcedon listing date, controversy, principal decision, and later dissent.

THEO.09.note: The Stanford entry surveys major theodicies and defenses while distinguishing attempts to explain evil from attempts to show logical compatibility.

exercise.prompt: Compare free-will, soul-making, and skeptical-theist responses to one concrete case of suffering, including the strongest objection to each.

THEO.10.note: Smarthistory connects theology, institutional conflict, vernacular scripture, visual culture, and print in a broad introduction to the Protestant Reformation.

exercise.prompt: Trace one Reformation dispute from the original church practice through Luther's objection, print circulation, political adoption, and Catholic response.

THEO.11.note: This joint Greek Orthodox Archdiocese and Hellenic Bible Society project introduces the Septuagint as the ancient Greek translation used widely in early Christianity.

article.title: About Septuagint.Bible
article.source: Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of America and Hellenic Bible Society

exercise.prompt: Compare one Old Testament quotation in the New Testament with its Septuagint and Masoretic Hebrew-based English forms, then describe the meaningful differences.

THEO.12.note: Stanford's philosophy-of-religion overview situates cosmological, teleological, ontological, moral, and evidential arguments alongside major objections.

exercise.prompt: Steelman one classical argument for God as numbered premises and a conclusion, then write the strongest objection and a possible reply.
